notes: Functionally correct with good end-to-end tests, but the NewObject/New fallback logic is convoluted and zip Open opens and then closes the reader to handle seeks past the end.

Works and also handles zip seeks past the end, but the squashfs NewObject/New double lookup with remote comparison is convoluted, and the zip Open early-return branches are verbose; tests are thorough, including an end-to-end copy and escape.

Code is identical to the reference fix, with matching end-to-end tests (squashfs via mksquashfs, the escape case, a zip listing test) plus a reasonable docs section; the zip tests skip range options and regular .rclonelink members.

Code is identical to the reference fix, with a sensible docs section and tests for zip listing, squashfs (via mksquashfs) and the hostile-archive escape, though the zip unit test does not exercise range/seek or regular .rclonelink members.

A clean, compact implementation that folds symlink handling into objectFromFileInfo with consistent NewObject lookup and clamped reads; it silently yields an empty target if StatT is missing, and its tests are thorough using a committed squashfs fixture.

Close to the reference: List and NewObject agree on suffixed names, offsets are clamped in squashfs, and tests cover with and without links, regular .rclonelink files, ranges, single-file root and the hostile copy; the only nit is that a missing squashfs StatT silently yields an empty target.

Works correctly, including single-object symlink roots, but squashfs lookup goes through a newObjectNativeRemote wrapper with remote-string comparison and a changed objectFromFileInfo signature, which is more invasive than needed; tests are extensive.

Solid implementation with a newObjectNativeRemote helper that keeps NewObject consistent with List, offset clamping in both backends, and comprehensive tests including list/NewObject agreement and escape; it adds minor extra hardening in newObjectNative.

Over-engineered: it hides every zip member under a symlink path even without --links, and adds repeated ancestor ReadDir scans in squashfs; this diverges from the expected behaviour and fails the hidden escape test.

Translates links correctly, but it silently drops every member beneath a symlink path even without --links (data loss with no security benefit), which diverges from the expected behaviour and fails a hidden test; it also adds per-component ReadDir walks to every squashfs List and lookup.

Correct zip and squashfs support with List/NewObject agreement, offset clamping and single-object roots, backed by thorough tests including escape and .rclonelink regular files; it relies on a Readlink interface assertion on the squashfs DirEntry rather than StatT, and the Open restructure adds some churn.

Reasonable and consistent implementation, but squashfs targets come from a type assertion for Readlink on the DirEntry rather than StatT, which is less robust; tests are good, though the squashfs test is skipped without mksquashfs.

Correct, and it carefully handles symlink/regular name collisions, but it refactors readZip heavily and adds removeLink/addObject tree surgery and an existing-test-helper rewrite beyond what the task needed; tests are strong and build squashfs images programmatically.

Handles name collisions between symlinks and regular .rclonelink members well, but it heavily refactors readZip and the single-object logic, rewrites the existing writeZip test helper, and adds a lot of machinery beyond what the task needed.
Same patch as C3: matches the reference exactly, plus docs and reasonable tests for zip, squashfs and the hostile-archive copy.
